newsitem.title: USA: Alaska forecasts rise in April hydrocarbon output.
newsitem.headline: Alaska forecasts rise in April hydrocarbon output.

text.p: Alaska's Department of Revenue on Tuesday said production of crude oil and associated gas from its North Slope fields could rise slightly in April, after maintenance and warm weather cut into March output.
Production of liquid hydrocarbons, which include oil and the gases captured with it, is forecast to rise by 8,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) over March to 1.376 million bpd.
But planned maintenance and forecasts of more warm weather could also lower April's output.
"You're going to see warmer weather...Our April projection could be a couple thousand barrels per day higher," said Chuck Logsdon, chief petroleum economist for the state of Alaska.
Warm weather decreases the efficiency of processors, which reinject natural gas into crude oil fields, increasing productivity.
March hydrocarbon output was 10,000 bpd less than expected, after water briefly clogged production equipment and six days of maintenance cut production at Prudhoe Bay, a key field.

Overall, production at Alaska's North Slope fields has begun to decline as fields grow older. Earlier forecasts pegged total May production at 1.36 million barrels, down from 1.424 million barrels in February.
